question: Does the printed 64-byte LP2-56 target consist of four consecutive MD5 digests of known preserved puzzle artifacts?

printed_target.source_field: reading.literal, the five hex runs each followed by a slash separator, between ampersand separators

block_rule: Decode the printed 128 hexadecimal characters to 64 bytes. Divide at byte zero into four consecutive, non-overlapping 16-byte blocks. MD5 the exact bytes of each unique frozen candidate once and compare the full 16 output bytes with each block in printed order.
controls: Validate MD5('abc') against the published standard value. In a synthetic 64-byte container, plant a known candidate digest at block zero and another at block three; recover both exact block indices and reject byte-reversed digests.
excluded: No unknown web-page search, arbitrary combinations of four candidate digests, changed candidate encodings, digest truncation, sliding offsets, reversed byte order, other algorithms or claim that this replays a historical proposal.
